diagnosis_explanation:
Your body has a condition called acute cholecystitis. This means your gallbladder got inflamed. Your gallbladder is a small organ under your liver. It stores bile, which helps you digest fats.

You recently had surgery to remove your gallbladder. This is called a laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

You have end-stage renal disease. This means your kidneys are not working well. You receive hemodialysis. This treatment cleans your blood.

You also have hyperlipidemia. This means you have high levels of fat in your blood. Hypertension is another condition you have. This means you have high blood pressure.

Congestive heart failure is also noted. This means your heart is not pumping blood as well as it should.

You had skin lymphoma five years ago. This was a type of cancer on your skin.

You have a thyroid problem called hypothyroidism. This means your thyroid gland does not make enough hormones.

Chronic bronchitis is also mentioned. This is a long-term condition that affects your lungs.
medication_rationale:
Synthroid 0.5 mg:
This medicine helps your body's energy level. It is for your thyroid gland. You may feel more energetic as it works. There are no common side effects to worry about. Call your doctor if you have a fast heart rate or feel very shaky.

Plavix 75 mg:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. Blood clots can block blood flow to your heart or brain. You may notice you bruise more easily. This is expected. Call your doctor if you see blood in your urine or have black, tarry stools.

Folic Acid 1 mg:
This medicine is a vitamin. It helps your body make new cells. You will likely not notice any changes as it works. There are no common side effects. Call your doctor if you have an allergic reaction like a rash or trouble breathing.

Diovan 80 mg:
This medicine helps relax your blood vessels. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood. You might feel less tired over time. Some people feel dizzy at first. This usually gets better. Call your doctor if you feel very lightheaded or have swelling in your face or throat.

Renagel 800 mg:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra waste. It is for your kidneys. You may notice fewer digestive problems like gas or bloating. Some people have an upset stomach or diarrhea. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you have severe constipation or a blockage in your intestines.

Lasix 40 mg:
This medicine helps your body remove extra salt and water. This can help lower blood pressure. You will likely urinate more often. This is normal and means it is working. Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy, have muscle cramps, or feel weak.

Lovastatin 20 mg:
This medicine helps lower your cholesterol. High cholesterol can block blood flow. You may not feel any different as it works. Some people get headaches or feel sick to their stomach. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you have muscle pain or weakness, or dark urine.

Coreg 3.125 mg:
This medicine helps your heart pump blood. It can also slow your heart rate. You may feel less short of breath. Some people feel dizzy or tired at first. This often gets better with time. Call your doctor if you feel faint or your heart rate slows down too much.

Nebulizer Therapy:
This treatment helps open up your airways. It can make it easier to breathe. You may feel relief from coughing or wheezing. Some people may cough more at first. This usually stops. Call your doctor if you have chest pain or trouble breathing that gets worse.

Phenergan 25 mg:
This medicine helps control nausea and vomiting. It can also make you feel sleepy. You will likely feel less sick to your stomach. Drowsiness is a common side effect. Try not to drive or use heavy machines. Call your doctor if you have confusion or feel very dizzy.

Pepcid 20 mg:
This medicine reduces the acid in your stomach. It can help with heartburn or an upset stomach. You may feel less discomfort in your stomach. Some people have mild headaches or feel dizzy. This is usually not a problem. Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain or black, tarry stools.

Vicodin 1 tablet:
This medicine helps relieve pain. It is for moderate to severe pain. You should feel less pain as it works. You may feel sleepy or dizzy. Try not to drive or operate heavy machinery. Call your doctor if you have breathing problems or feel confused.

Levaquin 250 mg:
This medicine is an antibiotic. It fights infections caused by bacteria. You should start to feel better as the infection clears. Some people have an upset stomach or diarrhea. This is usually mild. Call your doctor if you have tendon pain, rash, or trouble breathing.

Premarin - stopping:
Your doctor wants you to stop taking this medicine. It was stopped because of a higher risk of heart disease and stroke. Do not take it until your doctor tells you it is safe to start again.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and sore around your incisions.
- You can walk short distances inside your home.
- Do not lift anything heavier than 10 pounds.
- Eat foods that are easy to digest.
- Use your nebulizer every 3 hours if you need it.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 100.4 F.
- Your goal this week is to walk a little more each day.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy may slowly start to return.
- You can do light activities like sitting up and reading.
- Continue to avoid heavy lifting.
- Try to eat regular meals as you feel able.
- Use your nebulizer as needed for breathing comfort.
- Call your doctor if your pain gets worse or is hard to manage.
- Your goal this week is to walk the length of your hallway.

**Week 3:**
- You may start to feel less pain and more comfortable.
- You can increase your walking distance slowly.
- You can return to gentle household tasks.
- Continue to eat healthy foods.
- Use your nebulizer as needed.
- Call your doctor if you notice redness or swelling at incision sites.
- Your goal this week is to walk outside for a short time.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel more energy and less discomfort.
- You can resume most normal daily activities.
- Continue to avoid lifting heavy items.
- Eat a balanced diet to help your body heal.
- Use your nebulizer as needed.
- Call your doctor if you have new or worsening symptoms.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 15 minutes each day.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You will likely feel better each week.
- Healing takes time, so be patient with yourself.
- Continue to follow your doctor's instructions.
- Keep up with your regular check-ups.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Cannot breathe or gasping: Your body needs oxygen now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Signs of stroke: face drooping, arm weakness, trouble speaking.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: Apply pressure right now.
- Loss of consciousness or unresponsiveness: Call 911 right away.
- Seizure: Call 911 right away.
- Severe allergic reaction: throat or face swelling, trouble breathing.
- Signs of sepsis: high fever, fast heart rate, confusion, low blood pressure.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever above 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.
- Pain not helped by medicine: Your pain may be getting worse.
- Wound looks infected: red streaks, pus, or warmth.
- Cannot keep fluids down for 12 hours: You are getting too dry.
- Confusion or disorientation: This is a new problem.
- Sudden bad swelling in one leg: This can be a blood clot.
- Sudden weight gain of 2+ lbs: Fluid may be building up.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly getting better: You are healing well.
- Questions about your medicine or dose: Your nurse can help you plan.
- Wound healing slower than expected: Watch for signs of infection.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen as you heal.
- Nausea without vomiting: Try small sips of clear liquids.
- Fatigue that is improving: You are getting stronger slowly.
- Mild redness that is not spreading: Keep the wound clean and dry.
